statement:
For a scheme $T$ locally of finite type over a field $k$, $Z_n(T)$ is the group of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of Krull dimension $n$, and $\mathrm{CH}_n(T)$ is $Z_n(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $n+1$. If $A\subset T$ has dimension at most $n$, write $[A]_n$ for its cycle of $n$-dimensional components weighted by lengths of the local rings at generic points.

Let $k$ be a field, and let $X,Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $k$. Define exterior product on cycles by $[W]\times[V]=[W\times_k V]_{\dim W+\dim V}$ for integral closed $W\subset X$, $V\subset Y$, extending bilinearly, where $[W\times_kV]$ uses generic-point multiplicities even if this product is reducible or nonreduced.

For a morphism $f:T\to U$, a degree-$p$ bivariant class $c\in A^p(T\to U)$ consists of homomorphisms $\mathrm{CH}_n(U')\to\mathrm{CH}_{n-p}(T\times_UU')$ for all $U'\to U$ of locally finite type, compatible with proper pushforwards, flat pullbacks of fixed relative dimension, and Gysin maps for zero schemes of invertible-sheaf sections. Products of bivariant classes are composition of their compatible families after base change.

Let $X$ be smooth over a field $k$. Its diagonal $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow X\times_kX$ is a regular immersion and has a Gysin class $\Delta^!$. For schemes $U,V$ locally of finite type over $X$, define intersection of Chow classes by $\alpha\cdot\beta:=\Delta^!(\alpha\times\beta)\in\mathrm{CH}_*(U\times_XV)$; for $X$ smooth of pure dimension $d$, $\mathrm{CH}_n(U)\cdot\mathrm{CH}_m(V)\subseteq\mathrm{CH}_{n+m-d}(U\times_XV)$. For $U=V=X$ this defines the intersection product on $\mathrm{CH}_*(X)$.

For a local complete intersection morphism $f:U\to V$ that has a global factorization $U\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{g}V$ with $i$ a regular immersion and $g$ smooth, its Gysin class is $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$, independent of the factorization. A smooth $k$-morphism between smooth $k$-schemes is lci; the morphisms between smooth $k$-schemes in the statements below have such Gysin classes. On a regular closed immersion $i:W\hookrightarrow T$, $i^!$ is the Gysin pullback of bivariant intersection theory.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes smooth
over $k$. Then the Gysin map exists for $f$ and
$f^!(\alpha \cdot \beta) = f^!\alpha \cdot f^!\beta$.

\label{lemma-lci-gysin-product}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes smooth
over $k$. Then the Gysin map exists for $f$ and
$f^!(\alpha \cdot \beta) = f^!\alpha \cdot f^!\beta$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an integral scheme smooth over $k$.
Let $Y, Z \subset X$ be integral closed subschemes. Set
$d = \dim(Y) + \dim(Z) - \dim(X)$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim(Y \cap Z) \leq d$, and
\item $\mathcal{O}_{Y, \xi}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{Z, \xi}$
are Cohen-Macaulay for every $\xi \in Y \cap Z$ with
$\dim(\overline{\{\xi\}}) = d$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $[Y] \cdot [Z] = [Y \cap Z]_d$ in $\mathrm{CH}_d(X)$.

\label{lemma-intersect-properly}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an integral scheme smooth over $k$.
Let $Y, Z \subset X$ be integral closed subschemes. Set
$d = \dim(Y) + \dim(Z) - \dim(X)$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim(Y \cap Z) \leq d$, and
\item $\mathcal{O}_{Y, \xi}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{Z, \xi}$
are Cohen-Macaulay for every $\xi \in Y \cap Z$ with
$\delta(\xi) = d$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $[Y] \cdot [Z] = [Y \cap Z]_d$ in $\CH_d(X)$.

\label{lemma-intersect-regularly-embedded}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a scheme smooth over $k$. Let $i : Y \to X$ be
a regular closed immersion. Let $\alpha \in \CH_*(X)$. If $Y$ is
equidimensional of dimension $e$, then
$\alpha \cdot [Y]_e = i_*(i^!(\alpha))$ in $\CH_*(X)$.
